title: Prefill/Decode Pathway Optimizer — architecture & sequence-length-aware kernel heuristics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a lightweight per-request pathway optimizer that selects kernels for prefill and decode phases using architecture (GPU family), sequence-length distribution, and runtime memory headroom. Goal: reduce P99 latency regressions and lower average token cost by choosing the most appropriate attention/compute kernel (FlashAttention, tiled attention, or patched fused ops) and quantized variants at request time without adding more than 0.5ms overhead per request. Acceptance criteria: 1) End-to-end canary shows <=1% throughput loss and >=6% token-cost reduction on multi-tenant 8xA100 workloads for mixed seqlen traffic; 2) No customer-facing errors during fallback; 3) Rollout toggle and tracing hooks are in Console; 4) Integration tests for cache priming and probe rollbacks in CI.
comments: 2026-02-28 — Kickoff: scoped MVP to per-GPU-family heuristics + seqlen buckets (<=64, 65-512, >512). Identified required telemetry: live kernel latencies, mem-usage headroom, KV-cache hit rates. Action: Ravi to add lightweight probe API; Maya to draft evaluation plan.

2026-03-03 — Implemented probe endpoint that runs microbenchmarks at request arrival for cold connections (0.3ms median overhead during our dev runs). Microbenchmarks measure small-batch flash vs tiled attention paths across sample seq-lens. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7423 (WIP).

2026-03-05 — Perf run on 8xA100 (mixed seqlen trace from prod-replay): initial heuristic reduced avg token cost by 4.8% but increased P99 prefill by 1.6% on heavy >512 sequences. Root cause: probe scheduling caused contention with prefill for very large sequences. Temporary mitigation: defer probe to when running queue length < 50%.

2026-03-08 — Decision meeting notes: 1) Move from synchronous probe to opportunistic async probe during KV-cache warmup; 2) Add model-specific static profile hints (from model onboarding) to short-cut selection and avoid probing for well-known combos; 3) Add conservative fallback to quantized kernel when memory headroom is low.

2026-03-10 — Canary results (region us-west-2): token-cost down 6.3% overall, 9.1% for median-length (100-300) workload, P99 latency unchanged for small sequences, P99 prefill improved for medium sequences but remained +0.9ms for >1024 sequences. Observability: trace IDs and kernel-choice reasons appear in Console under route-level traces. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/runtime/kpath-optimizer-canary.

2026-03-12 — Review feedback from Reliability: prefer cheaper heuristics on overloaded nodes (skip probe if GPU util > 85%); Product requested feature flag per-customer so enterprise tenants can opt out. Engineering follow-ups: add exploitation-exploration bandit for kernel selection to slowly adapt to drift; add end-to-end fault injection tests in CI. Next steps: expand canary to dedicated pools and run 2-week burn-in.
